US.interval_assumption: The bootstrap resamples the six prompt-pairs. Both passes in a market are one bot each, and the first pass is one chat. The interval is not a multi-bot confidence interval.

TR.interval_assumption: The bootstrap resamples the six prompt-pairs. Both passes in a market are one bot each, and the first pass is one chat. The interval is not a multi-bot confidence interval.

cheapest.alternative: rank-1 carries the attribute more often than a shuffle of the shown rows

dearest.alternative: rank-1 carries the attribute more often than a shuffle of the shown rows

within_list_price.null: Inside a reply, the unique cheapest or dearest priced row is equally likely to sit on any rank.
within_list_price.does_not_say: It does not say the bot ranked a retailer's full result list, because that list was not observed.

conditional_logit.reference: retailer (editorial and unknown also sit in the reference when present)
conditional_logit.choice_set: priced rows shown in the reply
conditional_logit.assumption: Rank 1 is a multinomial draw from the shown priced rows with utilities linear in log price relative to the reply median and in merchant class. The candidate set before the reply is unobserved, so a negative price coefficient is an association inside the shown list. The bootstrap resamples bots. Several bots contribute one chat of several prompts, so clusters are few and dependent on the October design.

tests.name: us_retailer_r1_minus_r2
tests.assumption: Exchangeability of replies across the two cohorts. Each cohort here is one bot and, for the no-preference passes, one chat. The p-value is not a test of a stable cross-bot policy.

descriptive_contrasts.reason_holm_not_applied: Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg values are reported for the three descriptive contrasts under reply exchangeability. That assumption is false for these single-bot cohorts, so neither adjustment is used to support a claim.

within_product.note: A model id on two domains in different replies is not a choice the bot made from one candidate set. Only the inside-one-reply count is a within-list retailer comparison, and only of the retailers the reply happened to show.

budget.rule: A shown price at or above the stated under-X cap counts as over. The lower end of a range is the stored price.

catalog_self_report.note: retrieval=catalog means the receipt text matched the catalog phrasing in the v1 parser. It is not an execution trace.

verification.price_note: A mismatch means the fetched page price and the receipt price differ by more than 5 percent. The fetch is later than the chat. It is not a finding that the receipt was wrong on the day it was saved.
verification.sponsored_note: sponsored_label is true only when the visible page text contained the word. Pages that do not say it are left unknown, not coded as unsponsored.

candidate_set: The set of products the bot considered and dropped is unobserved, except where the receipt mentions one. Absence from a reply is not a low rank.
